title: From Peer Pressure to Purpose
subtitle: Nagpur Maharashtra’s Prakash Londhe’s Journey towards Self-Reliance
body_text:
Timely counselling, rehabilitation and behavioural support can play an important role in helping individuals overcome harmful influences, rebuild their confidence and return to productive livelihoods. Targeted support can also help beneficiaries regain focus, strengthen family financial stability and move towards a more disciplined and self-reliant life.
At 23, Prakash Londhe (name changed), a Scheduled Caste beneficiary from Nagpur, Maharashtra, was struggling with the negative influence of a peer group. The situation affected his routine and distracted him from his auto-rickshaw business, resulting in irregular working hours, missed peak-hour commuters, poor daily earnings and financial instability. His family was deeply concerned about his future and the economic difficulties caused by his inconsistent income.
Seeking to break free from harmful habits and regain focus on his livelihood, Shri Londhe received support under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) at Navjeevan Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addict, Nagpur, an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA). The intervention provided professional psychological counselling, motivational sessions, behavioural support, rehabilitation assistance and peer-refusal training to help him resist negative influences.
Through counselling and behavioural support, Shri Prakash developed greater awareness of the harmful effects of bad company and substance abuse. With continued guidance and emotional support from his family, he successfully cut ties with the negative peer group and adopted a more disciplined routine. He is now focused on operating his auto-rickshaw business regularly and making better use of peak-hour demand.
By working full-time and targeting peak rush hours, Prakash Londhe has seen a significant improvement in his daily rides and income. The improvement has helped stabilise his family’s financial condition and strengthened his confidence in pursuing his livelihood.
Prakash Londhe’s journey demonstrates how counselling, rehabilitation and family support can help an individual overcome negative influences, regain focus and move towards greater economic self-reliance. His experience reflects the importance of timely support under NAPDDR in enabling beneficiaries to rebuild their lives with discipline, dignity and renewed purpose.
